test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 14 Mar 2021 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following British policies triggered people to assemble at Jallianwala Bagh, Amritsar?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Rowlatt Act**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Rowlatt Act, also known as the Anarchical and Revolutionary Crimes Act of 1919, was passed by the British government in India in March 1919.
 
• The act gave the British authorities the power to imprison any person suspected of terrorism living in British India without trial for up to two years.
 
• The act also allowed the British government to stop the press from reporting and to arrest individuals suspected of sedition without a warrant.
 
• The widespread anger against the Rowlatt Act led to a series of protests and gatherings, which culminated in the tragic Jallianwala Bagh massacre.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Government of India Act 1919**

 
 
• This act introduced a dual mode of administration, called dyarchy, in the provinces of British India.
 
• It was part of the Montagu-Chelmsford reforms and aimed to increase the participation of Indians in the government.
 
• The act divided the subjects of administration into two categories: transferred and reserved subjects.
 
• While transferred subjects were to be administered by ministers accountable to the Legislative Council, reserved subjects were to be administered by the Governor and his executive council.
 
 
 
• **Simon Commission**
 
 
• The Simon Commission, formally known as the Indian Statutory Commission, was a group of seven British Members of Parliament under the chairmanship of Sir John Simon.
 
• It arrived in India in 1928 to study constitutional reform and make recommendations.
 
• However, the commission faced a widespread boycott because it did not include any Indian members.
 
• The commission's arrival led to protests and further fueled the demand for self-rule in India.
 
 
 
• **The Pitts India Act 1784**
 
 
• This act was passed to address the shortcomings of the Regulating Act of 1773.
 
• It established the dual control of the British government and the East India Company over India.
 
• The act set up a Board of Control in Britain to oversee the civil, military, and revenue affairs of the company.
 
• This act is significant as it marked the beginning of British parliamentary control over the East India Company’s activities in India.
